message:
Ah: the activity (verb) versus the product of that activity (noun). Nice, subtle catch, since I'm going to be spinning that stuff out in the presentation. Writing-as-activity is labor, which both neoclassical and Marxian economists construct as scarce: I mean, that's the whole focus of the Marxian folks, and the neoclassicals will tell you all about opportunity costs and [marginal rates of substitution](/weblog/archives/2004/03/30/classroom-economics/). Obviously, the plagiarism policies (and copyright itself) are all about the product, but with the implication that by making the product valuable, they're attempting to make the activity valuable -- there's some legal decision that pointedly remarks upon the intent of copyright not being the protection of property but the furthering of the useful arts.

I need to go back to Bruce Horner and sort this stuff out.
